articleTitle: Flexible Circuits for Soft Robotics
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In today's rapidly evolving industrial landscape, traditional rigid industrial robots are increasingly unable to meet the demands of complex and variable tasks due to their limited deformability, significant fatigue wear, and poor thermal management. This paper explores the flexible circuit technologies designed specifically for soft robots and their innovative manufacturing processes, highlighting how these technologies can significantly enhance the adaptability and flexibility of robots to address existing challenges. We propose a method combining liquid metal conductive pathways with an elastic substrate island structure to create stretchable circuit designs that meet the needs of soft robotics.

articleTitle: Automated Knitting Instruction Generation from Fabric Images Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This paper proposes a deep learning method to generate knitting instructions from fabric images, reversing the traditional process of manual pattern coding. The instructions are based on the five-layer structure derived from knitting logic, consisting of a front label recognizable from the front real image and a complete label corresponding to the knitting programming. The approach is divided into two phases: the Generation Phase, where neural networks produce front label instructions, and the Inference Phase, where mesh-based logic expands these instructions into complete labels. We also introduce an optimized labeling method for Kaspar's dataset, improving the accuracy, scalability, and knittability of the generated instructions. This method simplifies the knitting process by automating instruction generation directly from fabric images.

articleTitle: Dynamic Simulation of MNPs Particles Removed from Vessels by Micro-Nanorobots
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In this study, a Spherical Magnetic Robot (SMR) was designed to remove Magnetic Nanoparticles (MNPs) particles from blood vessels by micro and nano robots, and was studied by dynamic simulation model. SMR is based on a miniaturized design that utilizes magnet drive and integrates a high permeability alloy material to achieve effective adsorption and transport of MNPs particles. In this study, multiphysics problems for vascular modeling, SMR design, motion control, and MNPs particle capture were integrated, and a simulation model was constructed using the COMSOL Multiphysics software. The results show that SMR shows excellent navigation accuracy and adsorption performance in the process of removing MNPs, which verifies the key role of high-precision magnetic field control in SMR motion and MNPs adsorption process.

articleTitle: Research on the Features of the Series Arc Fault Detection and Phase Selection Based on Singular Value Decomposition and Multi-scale Norm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Electrical fires caused by arc fault are very common. To effectively prevent the electrical fire accidents resulted by the arc fault and reduce the troubleshooting time, a feature extraction method of the series arc fault (SAF) detection and phase selection in the three-phase motor and frequency converter load circuit was proposed. First, the SAF experiments under different lines conditions were conducted by using the three-phase motor and frequency converter loads. Second, a reconstruction of attractor track matrix was constructed, and combined it with the singular value decomposition to enhance the fault features. Third, the features of the SAF detection and phase selection were extracted from the feature enhancement matrix by using the multi-scale norm. Finally, by employing particle swarm optimization algorithm to refine a support vector machine, a detection and line selection model for the SAF was developed. According to the test results, the detection and phase selection accuracy of the SAF in the three-phase motor and the frequency converter load circuit were 98.12% and 91.63% respectively. It can serve as a point of reference for the development of the industrial arc fault circuit breakers with the SAF phase selection function.

articleTitle: Development of Soccer Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This paper presents the development of soccer robots for the WRG (World Robot Game) competition. Two models of soccer robots are designed and developed following the rules of WRG competition. One model is designed for 4WD (wheel drive), and another one is designed for 2WD. The soccer robots are controlled using a Flysky FS-GT3B RC transmitter in wireless communication. System structure and software development for controlling movement of the soccer robot are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: High Dynamic Range Image Processing Techniques for Automation and Machine Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: High Dynamic Range (HDR) imaging has become a significant technological advancement in visual data processing, allowing for the capture of a wider dynamic range of luminance levels in images. This paper explores various HDR processing techniques and their potential applications in automation and machine vision. By using methods such as multiple image fusion, image registration, and tone mapping, the paper demonstrates how HDR processing can enhance visual data in automated systems, improving accuracy in environments requiring complex lighting conditions. This work applies HDR algorithms to real-world scenarios, showcasing their potential in industrial automation and robotics, where accurate visual data plays a crucial role.

articleTitle: Research on Imaging Detection of Defects in X-ray Oil and Gas Casings Based on MIT-MTT Combined Instrument
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: The paper aims to study the X-ray oil and gas casing defect imaging detection based on the MIT-MTT combination logging instrument. By reviewing and analyzing relevant domestic and international literature, the paper summarizes the principles, advantages, disadvantages, and applications of existing algorithms. The research, based on experimental data from the MIT -MTT combination logging instrument, indicates that X-ray-based defect detection algorithms, combined with the imaging of the MIT -MTT combination logging instrument, play a significant role in improving the accuracy, efficiency, and automation of oil well casing inspection. With the continuous development of deep learning and defect detection technologies, the field is expected to achieve more breakthroughs in the future.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV Maneuvering Targets Tracking Based on Mobility-Focused Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of autonomous tracking of multiple dynamic ground targets by multiple Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). The purpose of the multi-UAV system is to maintain continuous coverage of these moving targets. However, when the targets exhibit high mobility, it becomes challenging for the UAVs to effectively track them. To address this, we propose a Mobility-Focused Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MF-MADDPG) model to learn a cooperative multi-UAV policy for tracking multiple targets. Specifically, we focus on the mobility of the UAVs while tracking highly mobile targets and design a mobility reward function to describe the difference of mobility matching between the UAVs and the targets. Performance tests conducted in the Gazebo simulation environment, based on the Robot Operating System (ROS) and the PX4 autopilot, demonstrated that the proposed MF-MADDPG model outperforms the traditional MADDPG model in tracking highly mobile targets.

articleTitle: Automatic Reading System for Thermometer Verification Based on Image Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In order to improve the working efficiency and reading accuracy for glass liquid thermometer verification, an automatic reading system of thermometer was designed. On the one hand, the thermometer reading image was acquired after it automatically entered the reading window by the hardware; on the other hand, the image recognition and verification data processing were completed by the software. In the image reading recognition, an optimized image processing scheme was developed, the improved image tilt correction algorithm enhanced the reliability of thermometer tilt angle calculation; the gray stretch function and binarization algorithm were optimized and improved by the improved adaptive genetic algorithm to ensure to obtain the ideal binarization image; the combination of erosion and dilation algorithm got good image features while removing image noise, which provided ensure for the accurate reading; the verification efficiency was further improved by this optimized reading process. The experimental results show that the system can quickly and accurately recognize the thermometer verification reading, which also shows that the system can be effectively applied to the glass liquid thermometer verification.

articleTitle: Development of a Laser-based Measuring System for the Radius and Roundness of Stator
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: A stator measurement system based on laser displacement sensors was developed to solve the problems of low efficiency, human error, and data visualization of the manual measurement of the stacked core radius in the stator assembly process of hydropower stations. First, the mechanical structure of the stator measurement system is designed based on the principle of comparison measurement, and the measurement of the stator radius of any cross-section is realized through motion control of the mechanical structure. Second, based on the laser sampling data, a method of compensating for the measurement error caused by the center column and stator's eccentricity is proposed, saving the time required to install and adjust the center column. Then, a software system with the functions of data processing, display, and storage was developed based on Python. Finally, the stator radius and roundness field test is carried out based on the above process. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the radius and roundness measurements of the measuring system is 0.078 and 0.051 mm, respectively, which meets the demand for fast and accurate measurement of the stator radius and roundness.

articleTitle: Hardware Based Real-time Processing of Online Ultrasonic Data of Railway Wheel Cracks: Multi-Sampling Rate Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In the piezoelectric ultrasonic online flaw detection of railway wheels, the transmission efficiency of ultrasonic data is critical to ensure the real-time detection of wheel flaws. Due to the large number of train wheels to be detected, the hardware sampling frequency of the online flaw detection equipment is high, the amount of ultrasonic echo data is large, and the data transmission and analysis processing time is extended. To improve the data processing efficiency, it is necessary to convert the sampling rate of the ultrasound signal to change the original data volume. According to the actual detection requirements, this paper studies the decimation and interpolation algorithm of ultrasonic digital signals and realizes the sampling rate conversion in the Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), which reduces data redundancy and improves system transmission and processing efficiency. The effectiveness and reliability of the method are verified in practical applications.

articleTitle: Development Status of Linear Steering Gear for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: As the key equipment to control the flying attitude of UAV, servo actuator plays an important role in the control accuracy and safety of UAV. The performance of servo actuator directly determines the flight quality and dynamic quality of UAV. For unmanned helicopters, large fixed-wing UAVs and other types of UAVs, the steering gear not only needs to provide greater torque, but also faces greater vibration and impact from the outside world, so the performance of the steering gear is also put forward higher requirements. This paper mainly introduces the development status of linear servo actuator with high control precision and strong impact resistance. It is found that the linear servo has higher control precision and stronger impact resistance. The advantages and disadvantages of hydraulic linear steering gear and electric linear steering gear are classified and summarized, and it is found that electric linear steering gear has gradually replaced hydraulic steering gear in the field of UAV application more and more widely. The importance of the development of electric linear steering gear in the field of UAV in the future is put forward, which will play an important guiding role in the development of UAV technology in the future.

articleTitle: Efficient Residual Chlorine Tracking and Automated Neutralization System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In industrial applications, seawater is frequently utilized as a heat source for gasification, necessitating chlorination to prevent microbial fouling of equipment. However, leftover residual chlorine poses a risk of marine pollution. This design outlines an STM32 microcontroller-based automatic system for monitoring and neutralizing residual chlorine. The system continuously tracks chlorine levels and autonomously administers sodium sulfite to neutralize excess chlorine. The hardware integrates modules for residual chlorine detection, flow rate measurement of the metering pump, motor driving, and signal conversion. The software framework includes systems for regulating chlorine concentration, monitoring pump flow rates, and controlling motor operations. Tests validate that all modules perform well, ensuring the system runs smoothly, efficiently manages residual chlorine, and safeguards the marine ecosystem.

articleTitle: A Practical HCI Evaluation Approach of Flight Deck
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: To evaluate the Human-Computer Interface (HCI) of the flight deck effectively and thoroughly, a practical evaluation approach of flight deck has been proposed. This methodology involves conducting a series of crew-task-based human factors evaluations, and has gained widespread acceptance in both the design and iterative phases of flight deck. Through extensive practical application, this approach has demonstrated its importance and practicality, particularly in identifying potential human factors issues and analyzing design optimization requirements. It facilitates iterative upgrades of cockpit design during the initial stages effectively, thereby preventing potential human factors issues and ensuring design optimization and improvement.

articleTitle: A Human Factors Validation Methods Incorporating the Degrees of Novelty, Complexity, and Integration of Cockpit Design Items
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This paper introduces a comprehensive Human Factors validation framework for CS25.1302 regulation, explaining how the degrees of novelty, complexity, and integration impact the level of scrutiny required for aircraft cockpit design items. The background underscores the role of human factors consideration for new, complex, and integrated designs in aircraft cockpit. The study aims to provide designers and regulatory authorities with a systematic methodology for determining appropriate means of compliance tailored to the varying degrees of novelty, complexity, and integration of design items. This method outlines the process of selecting a reference aircraft, participants, criteria employed, and how to carry out the assessment. Furthermore, it proposes the framework for selecting appropriate means of compliance considering the level of scrutiny supported by a case study. This framework not only optimizes the Human Factors evaluation procedures but also develops more reasonable scrutiny strategies. This, in turn, contributes to the overall enhancement of cockpit design safety and reliability.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of VGA Image Transmission Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: With the increase of image data scale, a faster and more efficient image acquisition and processing system is needed. FPGA has good parallel performance, which is very suitable for algorithms dealing with basic parallel features, and can greatly improve the efficiency of image acquisition and processing system. Aiming at the problem of FPGA image acquisition, processing and display, this paper carries out the design of real-time image acquisition system, which has the function of real-time display after processing the acquired image. In this paper, the chip of EP4CE6F17C8 of Cyclone IV series is used, the CMOS camera is OV5640 and the monitor is VAG. After full experimental verification, the system is extensible, the later expansion goal can not be achieved without the cooperation of Bluetooth and other facilities, with the role of recognizing and positioning license plates, obviously this series of application prospects are considerable; With flexibility, can customize the algorithm for optimization; Low cost a series of advantages.

articleTitle: Multimodal Physiological Signal for the Diagnosis of Parkinson's Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, characterized by a complex etiology and diverse clinical presentations. The intelligent diagnosis of this condition poses a significant challenge. Despite abnormal electrocardiogram (ECG), respiratory (RSP), and pulse signals in PD, which are closely linked to clinical symptoms, there remains a dearth of intelligent diagnostic models centered on multimodal physiological signals. In this study, we gathered multimodal physiological data from 55 PD patients and 30 healthy individuals, comprising ECG, photoplethysmogram (PPG), and RSP. Subsequently, we proposed a random forest classification model employing averaging probabilities, achieving an 89.41% accuracy in distinguishing between PD patients and healthy controls. Moreover, a feature ranking analysis was conducted on the time-domain features across the three modalities. This analysis unveiled the significance of time-domain features from diverse physiological signals in identifying PD, leading to optimization of the classification model and ultimately attaining a classification accuracy of 90.59%. In addition, the pulse and breathing characteristics in the open eyes state contribute more to disease identification, while the closed eyes state is mainly based on ECG characteristics. This research underscores the potential of machine learning techniques in amalgamating multimodal physiological data to enhance the diagnostic precision of PD, offering an objective and efficient clinical diagnostic approach.

articleTitle: A New Efficient Classification Method for Monkeypox Virus Skin Lesions Based on MPFormer
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Monkeypox is a serious zoonotic disease caused by the monkeypox virus. Traditional laboratory detection methods are time-consuming and have high biosafety requirements; in particular, electron microscopy is expensive and complicated to operate. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel classification algorithm for monkeypox virus skin lesions based on the Vision Transformer-MPFormer. We adopted a transfer learning strategy to train the MPFormer model on a monkeypox virus skin lesion dataset for accurate classification. Experimental results on the MSLD dataset demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves significant performance improvements compared to common models and other classification algorithms, with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score reaching 97.78%, 97.88%, 97.78%, and 97.78%, respectively. This study provides an efficient computer-aided diagnostic tool for rapid and accurate detection of the monkeypox virus, offering important practical application value.

articleTitle: Development and Implementation of a 6-DOF Robotic Arm with Machine Vision for Sorting Application
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: The automation of sorting tasks has been essential for various industrial applications, and this study focused on developing a 6-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) robotic arm to accurately sort objects through QR code scanning. The researcher conducted 40 trials across four distinct sets, categorized by color (red/blue) and size (small/large), obtained from a comprehensive functionality test. This study used sorting time as the dependent variable, while the independent variables are the four sorting categories analyzed through Analysis of Variance (ANOVA). The results revealed no significant differences in sorting times among the four sets, indicating that the robotic arm performed consistently across all categories. This finding demonstrated the robotic arm's effectiveness, accuracy, and flexibility in handling variations in object attributes such as color and size. The study concluded that the developed 6-DOF robotic arm, combined with machine vision technology and advanced control algorithms, was a reliable and efficient solution for small-scale automated sorting applications, making a valuable contribution to the advancement of robotic systems in industrial automation.

articleTitle: A Kinematic Parameter Identification Method Based on Auxiliary Variable for Industrial Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Accurate kinematic parameter identification is essential for enhancing the positioning accuracy of industrial robots. Traditional methods often struggle with poor convergence when faced with large initial parameter errors or noisy data, primarily due to the nonlinear nature of trigonometric functions involved in modeling joint angles and twist angles. In this paper, we present an auxiliary variable method that addresses these challenges by introducing auxiliary variables for the trigonometric terms. This transformation simplifies the nonlinear optimization problem into a linear one with equality constraints, making it more robust under challenging conditions. We establish the theoretical foundations of this approach and validate its effectiveness through simulations using a six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) robot model. The simulation results demonstrate that the auxiliary variable method significantly improves the robustness and reliability of parameter identification, particularly when large parameter errors and noise are present. The proposed method holds the potential for enhancing calibration accuracy in real-world industrial applications.

articleTitle: Qasync: A Dual Network Architecture for Value Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In this work, we propose Qasync, a novel dual network framework for value-based multi-agent reinforcement learning, aimed at addressing the control decision-making issues of Connected Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) in merge scenario. The core contributions of Qasync include the following two aspects: 1) Qasync extends QMIX by integrating a feedforward network, which reduces the limitations of QMIX's linearity assumption. 2) Qasync introduces a periodic mixing mechanism that combines Q-values from both networks, enabling Qasync to better capture non-linear relationships and enhance agents' exploration of diverse strategies. We evaluated Qasync using the SMARTS platform in a mixed traffic merging scenario, where autonomous vehicles must merge onto a two-lane road from a slip road, interacting with vehicles that randomly generated at the starting point to simulate realistic traffic conditions. Qasync was compared against several value-based baselines, including VDN, QMIX, and QTRAN, achieving average merging success rates of 80%, 89%, and 94%, respectively. Qasync achieved an overall merging success rate of 95%, demonstrating its ability to effectively handle complex traffic interactions and highlighting its potential for enhancing autonomous driving systems.

articleTitle: Human-Robot Interaction: A ROS2-Based Approach with Voice and Vision Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This project enhances human-robot interaction (HRI) by incorporating cutting-edge sensory feedback systems, real-time processing, and an intuitive architecture. A modular, scalable system architecture, developed using ROS2, integrates voice and vision systems to enable robots to execute commands precisely and interact seamlessly with users. Key contributions of this research include the fusion of voice and vision capabilities, the creation of a real-time audio segmentation algorithm, and the design of a flexible state machine controller. These outcomes highlight the potential of advanced HRI technologies and lay a strong foundation for future innovations.

articleTitle: The PCA Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Causal Relationships
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Fault diagnosis is a critical and central issue in industrial engineering, essential for addressing problems encountered in engineering systems. In recent years, data-driven fault diagnosis methods have gained extensive attention and application. Traditional fault diagnosis techniques primarily focus on analyzing data from individual fault nodes, making it challenging to capture the causal relationships between fault nodes accurately. This paper proposes a fault diagnosis method based on the combination of principal component analysis (PCA) and Liang-Kleeman Information Flow (LKIF). This method quantifies causal interactions between nodes by introducing information flow, thereby enhancing diagnostic efficiency. To validate the effectiveness of this approach, we conducted simulation experiments using the Tennessee Eastman Process (TEP) as a testbed. Specifically, we analyzed two faults in the TE platform and designed comparative experiments by varying two input variables. The results demonstrate that the LKIF-PCA fault diagnosis method achieves high accuracy, indicating its potential for practical applications.

articleTitle: Simulation and Optimization of On-Die Termination Based on DDR5
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: With the continuous development of information technology, data is showing an explosive growth trend, and the huge amount of data requires higher requirements for fast transmission and stable storage. Double Data Rate Synchronous Dynamic Random Access Memory (DDR SDRAM) is often used as a cache space for massive data and has a wide range of applications in both industrial and civilian settings. The On-Die Termination (OTD) technology in DDR incorporates terminal resistors into the DDR chip to improve the signal integrity of the channel. DFE provides a good equalization scheme for DDR links. This article is based on the DDR5 protocol and builds simulation models under different configurations. Then, OTD optimization and DFE optimization are carried out under different configurations, effectively improving the performance of the DDR interface after optimization.

articleTitle: Automated Detection of Korean Melons Based on YOLOv10 for Use in Quadruped Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: The production of Korean melon, known as Chamoe, in South Korea faces significant challenges due to the decline of the rural labor force and the high labor demands of manual greenhouse harvesting. This study provides a critical step toward developing an automated Korean melon harvesting system using a quadruped robotic platform. This study focuses on the evaluation of a deep learning model, YOLOv10, for accurate melon detection in Korean greenhouse environments, which is a key component of the proposed automated harvesting system. We used YOLOv10, a state-of-the-art object detection algorithm, and the model was trained and tested on a custom dataset of Korean melon images. An NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU and an Intel Core i9-13900K (3.0-5.8 GHz) CPU running Ubuntu 22.04 were used for the performance evaluation. The YOLOv10-based model showed promising results, achieving a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.927 at an intersection over union (IoU) threshold of 0.5. This model is suitable for use in robotic systems where resources are limited due to its compact size of only 5.7 MB. The model used only 11 % of the GPU capacity for setup and 2–3 % for inference. This demonstrates its efficiency and potential for real-time applications.

articleTitle: Extraction of Weld Seam Centerline Based on Improved Canny Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Based on the analysis of characteristics in weld seam images, this paper proposes an improved method for detecting the centerline position using an adapted Canny algorithm, addressing issues such as susceptibility to noise interference and poor connection of strong and weak edges. Initially, adaptive median filtering and enhanced bilateral filtering replace traditional Gaussian filtering in the Canny algorithm. Subsequently, histogram analysis and Otsu's method are employed to adaptively select thresholds for the Canny operator. Finally, the Canny algorithm is utilized for extracting weld seam edges. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to Gaussian filtering, employing adaptive median and bilateral filtering improves Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) by 9.2145 dB and reduces Mean Squared Error (MSE) by 33.32819, indicating superior effectiveness in preserving image details and eliminating noise. Pratt's Figure of Merit (PFOM) and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) values approaching 1 further underscore the algorithm's enhanced precision.

articleTitle: Model Merging with Lightweight Fine-Tuning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Recently, model merging techniques have emerged as a solution for combining multiple models into a multi-task framework. However, merging often results in a significant drop in accuracy, necessitating fine-tuning to enhance performance. In this work, we refer to the performance of a model fine-tuned to convergence as the model potential, decided by which error basin model lies on when initialized. We identify that prior research on model merging has primarily focused on the performance of the merged model rather than its fine-tuned performance, and this oversight suggests that a better-performing merged model does not guarantee has better model potential. To address this issue, we propose a novel model merging method that facilitates better integration of knowledge from Model A and Model B, thereby enabling superior model potential. Specifically, we conceptualize the parameters of the merged model as a linear combination of those from Model A and Model B, allowing us to optimize the linear combination parameter (LCP) through training. To mitigate random fluctuations, we typically initialize the LCP at 0.5, ensuring that the initial merged model does not exhibit a preference for either Model A or Model B. Comprehensive experimental comparisons demonstrate that the features of Model A and Model B are more effectively combined with lightweight fine-tuning of the LCP.

articleTitle: One-Handed Gesture Recognition Based on Improved ST-GCN and CA Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: The article takes one-handed gesture video as the research object, and mainly focuses on the recognition process and method of “isolated words” and static gesture mixtures. Firstly, the algorithm of extracting the key point positions of frame pictures is proposed by grouping rules of frame sequences of different gestures. This algorithm solves the problem of invalid gesture images affecting the recognition due to the redundancy of gesture images when extracting gestures from traditional gesture videos. Finally, a new network (ST-GCN-CA) is proposed, which improves the traditional spatio-temporal graph convolutional network (ST-GCN) and adds the CA attention mechanism. The method and network in this paper are applied to the Chinese isolated word sign language dataset (CSL-500) single-handed video, and the experimental results show that the recognition accuracies in the isolated word gesture video and the hybrid video reach 94.3% and 94.1%, respectively, which improves the recognition accuracies in comparison with other methods in the public domain.

articleTitle: Students' Attitudes Towards the AI-Based Automated Essay Scoring System: An Influencing Mechanism from Perceived Interactivity to Criticism
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has penetrated our lives by way of web search engines and mobile applications. AI-based Automated Essay Scoring (AES) is playing an increasingly important role in the field of education. This study explored the relationship between students' perceived interactivity of AES and their individual innovativeness as well as their reflective thinking about AES, and how these variables influence their criticism of AES. This study employed Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) for the data analysis. Valid data were collected from 442 students (40.05% male, 59.95% female, average age= 19.7) who had experience of AVE in private universities in China. The findings showed that: (a) Students' perceived interactivity of AES positively affected their individual innovativeness and reflective thinking about AES; (b) Students' individual innovativeness of AES positively affected their reflective thinking and criticism of AES; and (c) Students' perceived interactivity and reflective thinking about AES did not positively affect their criticism of AES. The findings not only revealed students' attitudes towards and experiences of this technological tool, but also provide valuable support for enhancing teaching effectiveness and improving teaching methods.

articleTitle: Research on Application of Stewart Platform in Uniform Scanning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: The space spectral imaging camera is planned to use a Stewart 6-DOF platform to drive a mirror for scanning and imaging, which requires the accuracy of the platform to reach the order of arcsec under the condition of multi-struts dynamic coupling. A Stewart platform realizes high angle resolution mainly by designing high-resolution linear driving struts. The resolution index of the 6-DOF Stewart platform is 2”, which needs the struts to achieve a high resolution of 60 nm. Based on this requirement, a driving strut with 50 nm resolution based on BLDC motor, ball screw, grating ruler is designed, which effectively ensures the high resolution of the platform. The transfer function of the single drive strut is identified by time domain method, and the closed-loop control model of the single drive strut is established. The dynamic performance of the single drive strut is simulated and analyzed. Finally, the dynamic performance of the 6-DOF scanning platform is experimentally studied. The experimental results show that the angular resolution of the 6-DOF Stewart platform is 2”, the swing angle range of the constant speed scanning is −1~1 degree, the nonlinear error of scanning angle in place curve is less than 0.2%, and the rotational speed is adjustable from 40”/s to 1800 ”/s, all the indicators meet the design index. This research has laid a solid foundation for the aerospace application of Stewart Parallel Platform.

articleTitle: Active Lateral Riding Comfort Control Strategies of High-Speed Train
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Based on the lateral vibration control of bogie frame for improving hunting stability in high-speed trains, three control strategies including linear quadratic regulator (LQR) control, Fuzzy Proportional-Integral (Fuzzy-PI) Control and Particle Swarm Optimization Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PSO-PID) Control are compared in this study. For the simplified linear lateral dynamics model of single bogie, the control parameters under the three control strategies are acquired, then they are applied to the vehicle dynamics model co-simulated by the SIMPACK and MATLAB codes. The different train operating conditions are taken into account and the improvement of dynamics indexes under the three control strategies are evaluated from the aspects of lateral riding quality of the car body and lateral force of wheelsets. The results show that the three control strategies lead to obvious mitigation on lateral vibration, and the improvement of PSO-PID control is the most obvious, but the LQR control effect is the worst.

articleTitle: Intersection Feature Analysis and Signal Control Optimization Based on VISSIM
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This study aims to enhance the traffic efficiency at the intersection of South Science Park Middle Street and North Anxiang Road, as well as the intersection of West Science Park Middle Street and South Science Park Middle Street through comprehensive analysis and simulation optimization. The research initially conducted a detailed organization and analysis of traffic flow data at both intersections, clarifying the traffic characteristics and existing issues at each approach. A traffic simulation model built with Virtual Interactive Simulation of Transportation Systems was used to assess the current traffic organization and signal timing, and a series of optimization measures were proposed, including improvements in traffic channelization, signal timing optimization, design improvements of traffic signs and markings, and the design and implementation of traffic detection and monitoring systems. The results of the study indicate that the proposed optimization measures can effectively reduce vehicle delays and queue lengths, enhancing the capacity of the intersections. Additionally, the study explored the design of traffic data detection and monitoring systems, providing technical support for real-time traffic management. Ultimately, the outcomes of this research not only provide a scientific basis for the traffic improvement of the two intersections but also offer a reference for addressing similar urban traffic issues.

articleTitle: Space Launch Group Planning Technique for Manned Space Station Construction
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: The launch mission for manned space station construction is characterized by strong constraints of spacecraft orbit and launch site, as well as tight coupling between multiple launch missions. It is a huge challenge for space launch planning to meet the overall requirements of engineering for reliability, safety, and efficiency. The space launch group planning technique is proposed based on the constraints of space rendezvous and docking and the coupling relationship between space launches using different types of launch vehicles, within the background of manned space station construction. The objective is to design space launch programs that meet the requirements of reliability, safety and efficiency within the specified timeframe. First and foremost, the four-dimensional space launch group-planning diagram is designed using isochrones, referring to the in-orbit space station, two launch sites, and the aerospace manufacturing plants. In the second place, a reliability evaluation function based on reliability growth, launch opportunity increase and launch window lengthening is proposed. Additionally, a safety evaluation function based on emergency rescue launch, and a benefit function based on parallel operation of multiple launch sites is introduced. Finally, the feasibility of the technology proposed is verified taken the construction of Tiangong space station as an example. The result indicates that the launch mission group planning designed using the technology proposed is highly consistent with the engineering practice results.

articleTitle: Research on Control Strategy for Waist-assisted Exoskeleton
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In order to alleviate the muscle fatigue of industrial workers who undergo repeated, intensive waist motions, a waist-assisted exoskeleton control strategy is presented. Firstly, the assistance principle is introduced. Then, an overall control method for waist-assisted exoskeleton is proposed, in which the finite state machine algorithm is adopted to identify the human motion intention, and corresponding control strategies, where no assistance is provided in squatting state, a slightly smaller constant torque is given in maintaining state, a torque similar to the net joint torque curve is designed in the getting-up state, are put forward according to different needs in different phases of bending down to assist workers to lift up heavy objects, reduce muscle fatigue, and increase operation efficiency. The electromyogram test results showed that the exoskeleton can reduce the erector spinae muscle activity by a maximum of about 24.45%, and an average reduction of about 11.13%, showing a significant assistance effect.

articleTitle: Research on MPPT with Improved Perturb-observe Method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Since the output of photovoltaic cell changes with the light intensity and temperature of the environment, and the properties has a typical characteristic of nonlinearity, the maximum power point of the photovoltaic module must be tracked to improve the efficiency of photovoltaic power generation. The output characteristic of photovoltaic cell was analyzed at first in the paper, then the perturb-observe method was improved by introducing the fuzzy control, and impedance matching optimization is realized by the PI closed-loop control Boost circuit. Finally, simulation models of the relevant control algorithm were built in Matlab, and the result showed that the ameliorated control algorithm possesses higher speed and accuracy in MPPT by simulation analysis and contrast, so it improved the photovoltaic efficiency of electricity generation.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Control System for Robotic Goalkeeping Using YOLOv9 and Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a control system for a wheel-legged robot to function as a soccer goalkeeper. The proposed solution leverages a re-tuned, task-specific tiny YOLOv9 model to achieve a realtime balance between detection accuracy and speed. Using a depth camera, the system estimates the 3D position of a fastmoving soccer ball, while a two-phase path planning algorithm guides the robot to the optimal intercept point. To further enhance performance, the method mitigates noise interference during interception. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, showcasing the synergy between deep learning techniques and classical control methods for dynamic and real-time robotic tasks.

articleTitle: Application Research on Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance and Navigation of Intelligent Vehicle Based on ROS
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: The research and application of autonomous driving technology are rapidly entering a stage of vigorous development, in which dynamic obstacle avoidance navigation technology is the key to achieve autonomous driving. In this paper, an intelligent car based on ROS (Robot Operating System) is studied and applied for dynamic obstacle avoidance and navigation. This paper aims to use the laser radar, so that the system can sense the surrounding environment in real time, through the SLAM algorithm to build a map, and combined with advanced path planning algorithm. At the same time, it can achieve intelligent avoidance of dynamic obstacles for vehicles. In the process of navigation, in order to adapt to the dynamic environment, A * and TEB path planner algorithms are used by the system to select the optimal path to the target location, and at the same time, it can dynamically avoid obstacles, and finally through the test to ensure the rationality of the design. The experimental results show that the global path planner and TEB local path planner can realize the dynamic obstacle avoidance of intelligent vehicle in the process of navigation. This research can bring certain reference for the development and application of unmanned driving technology in the later period.

articleTitle: Research on Prevention and Management of Crew Errors in Aircraft Cockpit Design
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This research focuses on the prevention and management of crew errors in aircraft cockpit design. Crew errors pose a significant safety challenge in the aviation industry. Therefore, the motivation behind this study is to propose a comprehensive approach to reduce the occurrence of such errors and effectively address crew error incidents that have already occurred. First, the background introduces the impact of crew errors on flight safety, emphasizing their critical role in air traffic management and flight operations. Furthermore, the potential risks and safety hazards associated with crew errors are discussed in detail. The main objective of this study is to identify various types of crew errors and their potential consequences and provide corresponding prevention and management strategies. To achieve this, we conducted an extensive literature review, covering various aspects such as crew error cases, pilot training, and design improvements. The key contribution of this paper lies in providing a systematic approach to prevent and manage crew errors. We not only focus on improvements in human factors engineering and training but also explore the potential of new technologies and design innovations to enhance the performance and safety of pilots and crew members.

articleTitle: Teleoperated Mobile Robotic Manipulator for Rescue Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This paper introduces a teleoperated mobile robotic manipulator specifically designed for rescue operations. The system integrates a robotic manipulator, a mobile platform, a hybrid power system, an environmental perception system, and a teleoperation console, forming a modular and highly adaptable architecture. A key innovation is the Feedback Correction Loop, which improves manipulator control by mitigating issues like communication delays, workspace constraints, and packet loss. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of the framework, demonstrating that the system can execute tasks smoothly, continuously, and safely under teleoperation.

articleTitle: An Iterative Variable Step Error Compensation Approach for Enhancing Robot Trajectory Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In this paper, an iterative error compensation approach is analyzed and designed to improve trajectory accuracy of industrial robots. Advanced offline programming and robotic machining tasks require high trajectory accuracy of industrial robots, which is significantly affected by parameter inaccuracy, stiffness deformation, backlash, and so on. Such complicated coupling makes it impossible to model each factor separately, thus data-driven direct error compensation is the major solution to improve trajectory accuracy. Previous methods utilize external measurement equipment to obtain tracking error and rely on the error consistency assumption to compensate for the error by modifying the trajectory commands directly. However, such consistency assumption does not hold. Even a minor incremental modification of the initial commands can lead to unexpected influence on the robot's tracking performance, owning to unaccounted factors such as the robot's dynamic stiffness and natural frequency. This paper decomposes trajectory tracking errors based on servo encoder feedback and external laser tracker, and proposes a variable step error compensation scheme to improve tracking performance. Physical experiments are conducted on a standard 6 degree-of-freedom industrial robot to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results of various error compensation approaches are analyzed to draw a possible error correlation model, in order to account for the error inconsistency in the compensation process.

articleTitle: A Language-Prompted Model for Semi-Supervised Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Object detection is a cornerstone of computer vision and artificial intelligence. Despite the advancements made by previous methods, they typically focus on visual signals, often overlooking the potential benefits of integrating language descriptions. Large-scale pre-trained language models offer rich semantic understanding that can complement visual cues, yet their application in object detection remains underexplored. This paper proposes a novel approach: a language-guided model for semi-supervised object detection. Unlike conventional methods that rely solely on visual features, our approach integrates a language model to encode descriptive information corresponding to images. For annotated data, language descriptions are derived from ground truth, capturing object categories and precise spatial coordinates in coherent sentences. In addition to leveraging labeled data, our method utilizes pseudo-labels for language descriptions on unlabeled data, enhancing training efficiency and model generalization. Experiments on MS-COCO dataset validate the superiority of our approach, which outperforms competitive methods with fewer labels.

articleTitle: Design of an Intelligent Assisted Medical Robotic Arm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: With the continuous development of science and technology and the aging trend of population, the accuracy, efficiency and safety of medical and manufacturing services have been put forward higher requirements. As an important branch in the field of productivity development, the robotic arm provides assistance to the development of manufacturing and medical fields by integrating advanced automation, sensor technology and precise mechanical structure design. In this paper, we design a kind of intelligent medical robot arm, realize the control of robot arm through visual recognition and voice recognition function, aiming to improve the quality of medical service and manufacturing production, reduce medical cost, reduce the waste of human resources, and promote the innovation and development of medical technology.

articleTitle: The Design and Implementation of a Control Computer Based-on FPGA Core
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: According to the requirement of the system operation, a control computer monitors and controls a large number of key nodes, synthesizes a variety of excitation signals, obtains the angular state of the rotating mechanism, controls its rotation to the specified position. Based on an FPGA (Field-Programmable Gate Array) core, this paper develops a signal synthesizing module, a digital axis-angle conversion module and a W5500 Ethernet interface using a SOPC system that can be tailored and configured flexibly. It integrates the customed logic IPs into the SOPC (System-on-a-Programmable Chip) system of the Nios II architecture. The software system coordinates the operation of all modules. Finally, the control computer synthetically implements all its functions.

articleTitle: Tool or Partner: Mental-Aware Human-Robot Collaboration
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Human-robot collaboration is a critical area of research, aiming to maximize synergy between humans and robots. However, a fundamental question persists: Should robots be seen as mere tools or genuine partners? Existing experimental environments have limitations in supporting virtual human-robot collaboration studies. In this paper, we propose a novel robot training framework designed for mental-aware human-robot collaboration. Within this framework, we introduce a Trust-Aware Mental Model incorporating a Human Trust component to represent human trust in robots. We create a virtual simulation environment to evaluate this model and conduct human-robot collaboration experiments. Quantitative and qualitative analyses demonstrate that integrating the trust-aware mental model enhances collaboration effectiveness. This finding underscores the necessity of viewing robots as true human partners and provides valuable insights for future research in human-robot collaboration.

articleTitle: Exploring the Capability of Deep Neural Network on Ship Sub-Assembly Weld Seam Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: To address the problem of robot weld process planning for complex ship sub-assembly work-pieces, this paper explores the capability of the deep neural network models on seam cloud point segmentation tasks. By studying and leveraging the performance of three popular point cloud segmentation models, we choose PointNet++ as the backbone and introduce three improvements to enhance its performance on the weld seam segmentation problem. First, a multi-perspective edge detection method is proposed to improve segmentation accuracy. Second, neighborhood sampling and fast farthest point sampling are introduced to improve the sampling efficiency. Finally, we use fewer convolution layers to reduce the time and space complexity and resolve the overfitting problem. A dataset of sub-assembly models containing 4 plate type classes and 5 seam type classes was established. The training and recognition performance of the advanced PointNet++ model was evaluated and compared with the traditional geometrical weld seam recognition method. The experimental results prove that the proposed method can adapt to 5 typical weld seam classes at a mIoU 83.38%, and it is robust to arbitrary work-piece layout positions, meanwhile, it reaches a speed at 15fps. All the above results demonstrate the great potential of deep neural networks on the robot weld applications for ship sub-assembly work-pieces.

articleTitle: Gameplay Generation System Based on Game Description Language
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This study defines a specialized game description language, CCGDL, and develops an automated gameplay generation system called Creative Game Machine based on CCGDL. The system facilitates automated gameplay generation and quality evaluation by employing techniques like parent selection and rule crossover, ensuring controllable gameplay quality. Additionally, the study introduces a quantitative analysis method for gameplay quality, utilizing machine learning algorithms to predict gameplay quality. The system significantly reduces design cycles and development costs, demonstrating the potential to enhance traditional game design methodologies.

articleTitle: RELA: An Online-Offline Framework for Rules Enhanced Logs Analysis Based on Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have played a pivotal role in the field of Artificial Intelligence Operations (AIOps), particularly in the analysis of log data. However, the use of open-source LLMs for automated log analysis often falls short of expectations in offline environments in practice. To address these challenges, this paper introduces an innovative Online-Offline framework named RELA to enhance the performance of LLMs in log analysis. In the online phase of our framework, GPT-4 meticulously analyzes logs to determine the presence of anomalies and deduces rules based on these determinations, which are then compiled into a comprehensive rules base. In the offline phase, open-source LLMs leverage this rules base to significantly enhance the effectiveness of log analysis by retrieving the most applicable rules. To validate the effectiveness of our proposed framework, we meticulously annotated a dataset specifically designed for a distinct offline scenario, focusing on two primary tasks: the detection of log anomalies and the explanation of these anomalies. Our experimental results demonstrate that the implementation of the rules base leads to a 3% to 25.3% increase in the accuracy of anomaly detection. Additionally, assessments conducted by domain experts validate the improvements, highlighting a substantial enhancement in the credibility of the explanations provided by LLMs within this framework. These findings not only underscore the practicality but also the efficacy of our approach, establishing a solid foundation for further research and application in AIOps.

articleTitle: A Corrosion Detection Method for Hydraulic Metal Structures Based on an Improved YOLOv10 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: To achieve corrosion detection of hydraulic metal structures based on deep learning, reduce subjectivity in the corrosion annotation process, and enhance annotation efficiency, this study proposes a corrosion detection method for hydraulic metal structures based on a YOLOv10 serial architecture that incorporates a Transformer module. The serial architecture first uses an object detection model to locate corrosion, followed by a classification model to assess corrosion severity. In terms of F1-score, the proposed corrosion detection network shows a 1% improvement over the baseline. For accuracy, after transfer learning, the proposed corrosion classification model outperforms the baseline by 8.8%. This method was implemented in real-world scenarios, successfully enabling corrosion detection and severity classification of hydraulic metal structures, and verifying the feasibility of the serial architecture.

articleTitle: Human-Robot Collaboration Attack Based on Perception Deception
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Human-robot collaboration (HRC) plays a crucial role in various fields, highly relying on the perception capabilities of robots. While some literature explores HRC, research on potential attacks against HRC systems remains lacking. This research gap could lead to system vulnerabilities being exploited, affecting productivity and worker safety, and hindering the further adoption and application of HRC technology. We propose a perception-based deception attack method for HRC, which misguides the robot's perception to attack its decision-making, thereby impacting the effectiveness of human-robot collaboration. Our experiments involved a widely-used HRC task and demonstrated that perception deception could reduce the human-robot collaboration completion rate by over 36.67% and increase decision latency by 87.58%. The experimental results indicate that these attack methods can significantly reduce the robot's perception success rate. Through this research, we lay the foundation for further studies on improving the efficiency and robustness of human-robot collaboration.

articleTitle: Research on the Method for Formulating Power Spectral Density of Fuel Cell Vehicle Air Compressor Bench Based on Operating Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In order to obtain a load spectrum of fuel cell vehicle air compressors that is highly correlated with the actual usage scenarios of users throughout the entire lifecycle, this paper defines, classifies, and weight statistics the actual usage scenarios and conditions of users based on big data analysis of fuel cell vehicle operating conditions, and extracts key data information. The main technical route of the research includes the following steps: Firstly, road load data collection is carried out in various typical road driving scenarios and working conditions to obtain the excitation signals of fuel cell vehicle air compressors in different working conditions and scenarios, thereby forming statistically representative load samples. Subsequently, based on the weight information provided by the big data analysis of operating conditions, the load spectra of each operating condition and scenario are weighted and superimposed. By calculating the load spectrum, the fatigue damage spectrum (FDS) and corresponding power spectral density (PSD) of the air compressor are finally obtained, providing important basis for subsequent research and application.

articleTitle: Intelligent Simulation and Measurement of Dielectric Constant of Alumina in Terahertz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: As key parameters for calculating dielectric constant, including transverse and longitudinal phonon vibration frequency, loss factor, and high-frequency dielectric constant, this paper uses two methods, intelligent algorithm and first principles calculation, to calculate four parameters of alpha alumina at 300K, and compares and analyzes them with the measurement results of Fourier time-domain spectrometer (parameters, dielectric constant, and reflectivity). The comparison results show that both methods are in good agreement with the experimental results, but the accuracy of the intelligent algorithm is higher.

articleTitle: Design of a 1700V-300A 62mm SiC MOSFET Module
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: SiC devices possess characteristics such as high voltage resistance, low loss, and high thermal conductivity, making them highly advantageous for applications in smart grids, new energy power generation, and rail transit. This paper focuses on the design methodology of a high-power, high-voltage, and high-current module by designing a 1700V-300A 62mm SiC MOSFET module. Initially, the SiC MOSFET chip and SiC SBD chip were calculated and selected; subsequently, the layout and wiring of the SiC MOSFET module chip were designed using Solidworks software for physical modeling. Furthermore, Q3D software was employed to extract parasitic parameters of the model while establishing an equivalent circuit model of the SiC MOSFET module simulated through LTspice software. Finally, ANSYS software was utilized for thermal simulation analysis of the module's performance after conducting double pulse tests. The results show that the module in this paper has good performance and has certain application value.

articleTitle: Research on Cockpit Aviation Accident Analysis Model
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In exploring the design of regression models for aviation accident analysis, we need to focus on aspects such as model construction, parameter selection, data processing, and model validation. Aviation accident analysis is a crucial aspect of ensuring aviation safety. Through in-depth analysis of historical accident data, we can uncover the causes and patterns of accidents, leading to effective prevention and improvement measures. Among various analytical methods, regression models are powerful and flexible tools that can quantify the relationships between different factors and aviation accidents, as well as predict potential risks.

articleTitle: Design of Forest Fire Alarm System Based on GSM
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This project designed a smoke fire anti-theft alarm based on GSM, which can automatically detect smoke and flame, and send real-time alarm message to the user through GSM network, so as to improve the fault tolerance rate when the house is in danger of fire. The alarm mainly includes smoke detection sensor, human infrared detection sensor, control center, GSM module and power supply components. When smoke or flame is detected, the control center will send instructions to the GSM module, and the GSM module will send alarm information to the user's mobile phone.

articleTitle: Bifurcation Investigating of a Fractional Neural Networks Involving Incommensurate Delays
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In this current article, an issue of Hopf bifurcation control about a novel fractional-order network owing multiple delays and feedback gain is formulated. The bifurcation parameter time delay is selected as the bifurcation parameter. The stability conditions and the bifurcation point are established. Ultimately, a simulation example is provided to verify the validity of the obtained newly results. The important results obtained in this paper have important theoretical significance and application value for the regulation and control of fractional-order neural networks with time-delay.

articleTitle: Research on Matching Degree of Agricultural Landscape Based on UAV Space Ranging
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Agricultural landscape is a form of expression of the earth's landscape achieved through agricultural planting, usually presenting a design image of the earth with different types of plants working together. In the specific implementation process, due to spatial errors in plant planting, there are often some errors in the presentation of the final effect compared to the initial design image, which becomes an important factor affecting the appearance of the final effect. This article aims to use unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) spatial ranging technology to calculate the error values between agricultural landscape products and design patterns based on several feature points, comprehensively measure their presentation effects, and provide evaluation criteria for the planting quality of agricultural landscapes.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection Device for Ripple of Mine Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Power supply ripple, as one of the important indexes to measure the quality of power supply, has an important influence on the stability and reliability of mine electronic equipment. Because of its special working environment and load requirements, mine power supply puts forward higher requirements for the suppression and detection of power supply ripple. This paper expounds the generation mechanism of power supply ripple, analyzes the difference between linear power supply and switching power supply in ripple generation, and puts forward an automatic detection device for mine power supply ripple. The hardware of the device is highly integrated with high-precision detection equipment such as oscilloscope, source voltage and electronic load, and the software adopts virtual instrument technology to design an automatic detection system for mine power supply ripple. The experimental results show that the automatic detection device for mine power supply ripple has been improved in accuracy, stability and automation, which provides a more efficient and reliable solution for mine power supply ripple detection.

articleTitle: A Structure Design and Finite Element Analysis of a Dual Servo-Driven Gripping Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In response to the difficulties in grasping irregular objects and the single grasping angle issue of mechanical claws carried by small multi-rotor aerial vehicles, this paper takes the grasping mechanical claw carried by multi-rotor aerial vehicles as the research object and designs a four-finger mechanical claw driven by dual servos that can rotate. First, the mechanical claw model was established in SolidWorks, and then it was imported into ANSYS Workbench for static and transient dynamic analysis of the push-pull crank and meshing gears of the mechanical claw, obtaining the total deformation and stress distribution cloud diagrams of each component. The analysis results indicate that during the process of grasping objects, the maximum stress of the push-pull crank and meshing gears of the mechanical claw is far less than the material yield strength, and all meet the working requirements. This provides a reference for the design and optimization of similar structures such as mechanical claws carried by rotor aerial vehicles.

articleTitle: Fall Detection by 1D-CNN Based on Public Dataset Using a Wrist-Worn Smartwatch
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Falls among the elderly population pose a significant threat, often leading to severe injuries, loss of independence, and even fatality. To address this critical issue, researchers have been exploring various approaches to develop effective fall detection systems. In this study, we present a novel fall detection algorithm that leverages the WEDA-FALL dataset, a comprehensive dataset that includes data from wrist-worn sensors capturing both simulated and real-world fall incidents involving elderly individuals. The key insight behind our approach is the observation that falls often exhibit distinct patterns in sensor data. To capture these patterns, we employ a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) architecture, which has been shown to be well-suited for time-series data analysis. By training our model on the WEDA-FALL dataset, we were able to achieve an impressive accuracy of 94% in fall detection, surpassing the commonly reported accuracy levels of around 90% in the existing literature. The high performance of our algorithm can be attributed to the use of the WEDA-FALL dataset and the effectiveness of the 1D-CNN architecture in extracting and learning the characteristic patterns in the sensor data. Notably, our algorithm offers the key features of being quick, highly accurate, and cost-effective, making it a promising solution for practical deployment in real-world settings to improve the safety and well-being of the aging population.

articleTitle: Comparison of KAN, MLP, and SVM for NIR Spectra Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Near infrared spectra are typically high dimensional data and widely used in various industries and scientific areas. Various machine learning algorithms have been employed to classify the NIR spectral data. This paper compares the performance of three popular models: the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), in classifying Mah map datasets which are derived from preprocessed NIR spectra. This study investigates the performance of three prominent machine learning models Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Kolmogorov-Arnold Network Network (KAN), and Support Vector Machine (SVM), in classifying high-dimensional Near Infrared (NIR) data within the tobacco industry. The impact of hidden layer architecture on classification accuracy was examined for both MLP and KAN networks. While KAN demonstrated superior accuracy and stability with L-BFGS optimization, particularly when employing two hidden layers, it exhibited inferior performance with Adam optimization compared to MLP. With one hidden layer and same hidden neuron number, KAN can provide slightly better classification accuracy in high dimension than both MLP and SVM. However, SVM proved generally stable across various input dimensions, achieving high classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Design and Application of Communication Technology System for Mine Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This paper deeply discusses the present situation, development and application of communication technology of mine power supply. The communication technology of mine power supply plays a vital role in modern mining production. With the improvement of automation and intelligence in coal mines, the requirements for power supply and communication technology are increasingly strict. The harsh working environment under the mine, such as high dust, high gas concentration and high noise, poses a severe challenge to the stability of power supply and the reliability of communication. Therefore, this paper studies the communication technology of mine power supply, puts forward the system design and application of mine power supply communication technology, and gives a detailed explanation from hardware design to software design and system integration and testing. The test shows that the system improves the safety, efficiency and intelligence level of mine production, which is of great significance for ensuring the safety of miners, optimizing the energy structure and promoting the sustainable development of mines.

articleTitle: A Large-Scale Multi-objective Evolutionary Algorithm Based on Two-layer Encoding Scheme for Neural Network Training
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Evolutionary algorithms (EAs) have achieved great performance in solving multi-objective optimization problems (MOPs). However, there are more complex features in real-world MOPs. For example, the neural network training problem is characterized by large-scale decision variables and sparse Pareto-optimal solutions. This makes it difficult for most EAs to solve the neural network training problem. Therefore, this paper proposes a large-scale multi-objective evolutionary algorithm based on two-layer encoding scheme (MOEA- TES). In the proposed algorithm, the two-layer encoding scheme is employed. Moreover, a two-stage evolutionary strategy is designed for guiding the genetic operator. MOEA- TES is assessed by four real-world neural network training problems. Compared with five recent state-of-the-art algorithms, the proposed MOEA- TES achieves competitive results.

articleTitle: Research on Multiple Failure Analysis Method for Dynamic Reconfiguration Flight Control System of BWB Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: For the multifunctional configuration of control surfaces in the flight control system of BWB aircraft, and the complex redundancy management and reconfiguration capabilities implemented in the event of failures, a multiple failure analysis method based on multiple failure state space is proposed. Taking a certain type of BWB aircraft as an example, a failure relationship matrix is defined to automate the analysis of Failure combinations under different state spaces. The results show that this method can effectively analyze the evolution process of system failure states and safety impacts across different state spaces, systematically identifying failure modes and the processes of redundancy switching and reconfiguration.

articleTitle: Extremely Low Frequency Communications: Antenna Design, System Design, and Experimental Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Wireless communication is the main means of emergency rescue after a disaster. However, electromagnetic waves (EMWs) in commonly used frequency bands experience significant attenuation when passing through obstacles, and traditional extremely low frequency (ELF) antennas are too large to be carried by rescue robots. This paper proposes a new radiation mechanism, which involves changing the current in the solenoid to alter the magnetic field distribution around the solenoid, thereby enabling information loading. This solenoid antenna is capable of emitting a single-cycle sine pulse. To achieve ELF communication using this pulse, this paper presents a joint pulse position and shape modulation (JPPSM) scheme for the transmitter and a flexible delay synchronization (FDS) scheme for the receiver.
