FDS utilizes distributed pulses to ensure low redundancy and exploits the acquiring and tracking ability to adaptively increase delay to ensure synchronization accuracy. Simulations show that FDS has higher accuracy and faster acquisition than existing schemes. Experiments show that the operating frequency range of the solenoid antenna is from 14 to 165 Hz. The proposed ELF communication system is capable of achieving error-free transmission over a distance of 450 meters.

articleTitle: Calculation Method of Collision Probability for Airdroping Targets in Limited Space
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Airdropping relief supplies to disaster-stricken areas is one of the most effective means to implement rapid supply after major natural disasters. Due to the relatively small key disaster-stricken areas, the collision of airdrop targets in a limited space will make it difficult for relief supplies to reach the rescue area accurately, thus losing the value of airdrop. Starting from the general form of collision probability, this paper studies three numerical calculations: direct solution, two-dimensional integral and one-dimensional integral by transforming the three-dimensional probability calculation problem into the two-dimensional probability calculation problem in the vertical encounter plane. Numerical examples show that the results of the two kinds of integrals are relatively close, and they can be used to calculate the collision probability of airdrop targets in most cases, and the one-dimensional integrals are more advantageous without considering the factor of calculation efficiency; Based on the condition that the projected area is circular and the probability density does not change much, the direct solution can also be used to calculate the collision probability in general cases, but compared with the two-dimensional integral and the one-dimensional integral, the maximum calculation error is about 2.74% and 2.97% respectively; The two-dimensional integral calculation can be used to calculate the collision probability in most cases, and the calculation accuracy is relatively high. When considering the calculation efficiency factor, the two-dimensional integral calculation can replace the one-dimensional integral calculation. The conclusion of the study can provide support for the implementation of active evasion strategy of airdrop targets.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Optimization Model for Parcel Replenishment Delivery Based on Mobile Lockers
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This study addresses the replenishment delivery of packages received at the warehouse during the mobile lockers delivery process by establishing a two-stage optimization model. The first stage plans the delivery of parcels that arrived at the warehouse the previous day, while the second stage focuses on supply vehicles replenishing parcels that arrive during the delivery period. And the large neighborhood search algorithm is developed to solve the problem, and its accuracy and effectiveness are validated through numerical experiments. The results indicate that incorporating replenishment delivery significantly enhances customers' requirement for timeliness, with 400% to 600% of parcels successfully replenished on average. Additionally, replenishment contributes to substantial cost savings, reduces the travel distances of mobile locker, and decreases carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Dynamic Task Sequence Allocation Based on Natural Language Instruction
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In recent years, with the development of technology, robots have become more prominent in the public eye. Service robots are now being used in some smart hotels to decrease manual transportation costs. However, these service robots operate according to set instructions, and humans usually apply fixed operating instructions to control the robots. Whether in daily life or at work, humans are more likely to use natural language to communicate and give task instructions. Moreover, in the field of multi-robotics, most of the existing researches on multi-task assignment have been conducted in simulation environments on a list of pre-set tasks, and seldom update the task sequences in real time in conjunction with the real environmental information and time. In this paper, we propose a method for assigning dynamic navigation task sequences based on natural language instruction and verify its effectiveness in a real scenario.

articleTitle: Study on Point Cloud Processing Technology in Robotic Welding for Ship Sub-Assembly
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: To address the issue of insufficient automation in robotic welding for ship small assemblies, this study develops a welding technology based on point cloud processing. The research utilizes vision sensors to collect point cloud data of workpieces, and an improved point cloud processing algorithm is employed to extract weld seam information effectively. A novel real-time online calibration method for vision sensors is introduced, which precisely transforms the weld seam position from the vision sensor coordinate system to the robot coordinate system, thereby ensuring accuracy and continuity in the robotic welding process. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed technology significantly enhances automation and weld quality in ship small assemblies, showing substantial industrial application potential.

articleTitle: Text Input Through Swipe Gestures Based Personalized AI Agent
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Text input based on virtual reality is a common technique in interactive systems, but it may face challenges related to input efficiency and task load when interacting with VR hardware and applications. The development of artificial intelligence interaction technologies offers new approaches to addressing text input challenges. In this paper, we propose a swipe gesture-based text input method under a personalized AI agent framework, combining portable devices (e.g. smartphones) with VR input and incorporating user profile information, input habits, and conversational intent. By integrating the GPT-3.5 model to train a personalized AI agent, we emphasize the importance of understanding and responding to human behavior or capabilities from the agent's perspective, enabling text prediction based on specific contexts. The keyboard layout design is based on a disk divided into 8 equal regions, where the outer circle is subdivided into key areas containing letters, and the inner circle serves as the input buffer area. By resolving word ambiguities based on user input and leveraging the extensive capabilities of large language models in context awareness and text prediction, the system allows complete sentences to be generated from keywords. This reduces the number of manual inputs required by the user, improving text input efficiency and enhancing the overall user experience.

articleTitle: Development of Automatic Detection System for Explosion-Proof Test
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Explosion-proof electrical equipment can be divided into explosion-proof type, intrinsically safe type, pouring type and so on according to the explosion-proof principle, among which explosion-proof electrical equipment is the most widely used. Explosion test is the basis for judging whether flameproof electrical equipment can meet the standard requirements and can be used in explosive dangerous environment. In order to test the explosion-proof performance of flameproof electrical equipment, a set of flameproof test and detection system is developed, which consists of explosion test tank and control system. The test results show that the system realizes the automatic control of explosion test of flameproof electrical equipment shell, and the detection data is reliable and the detection efficiency is high.

articleTitle: Enhanced CBBA with Multi-Condition Evaluation for Multi-Robot Collaborative Exploration
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In multi-robot collaborative exploration of unstructured environments, redundant exploration often occurs, leading to significant consumption of computational resources and thus reducing exploration efficiency. To address this issue, this paper proposed the EC-MCE algorithm, an enhancement of the Consensus-Based Bundle Algorithm (CBBA) algorithm, which integrates a fully connected neural network to evaluate five key factors: travel cost, information gain, loop closure likelihood, revisit probability, and deviation for local benefit evaluation. This approach ensures the efficient allocation of boundary points, which in turn ensures the efficient completion of exploration tasks. The effectiveness of this method was verified on the Airsim simulation platform, with experimental results showing that compared to traditional methods, this approach reduced the total exploration time by about 10% and decreased the number of repeated area explorations by about 20%. These improvements significantly enhance the exploration efficiency of the system while ensuring the safe navigation of multiple mobile robots in unstructured environments.

articleTitle: The Aircraft Assisted Driving Method Based on Machine Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This electronic Monitoring the changes in various flight data during aircraft operation is crucial for ensuring safe flight. Currently, most aircraft are equipped with on-board monitoring software that can obtain real-time flight data during operation. When problems occur with the aircraft or the pilot performs abnormal operations, it will trigger warnings of different levels. In addition, the use of satellites, radars, and other equipment allows for the collection and analysis of flight data of aircraft in operation on the ground to predict potential risks. The pilot's operation plays a vital role in flight safety, and there are misoperations caused by human factors when the pilot is operating the aircraft. Aircraft instruments provide a lot of information, and if the pilot needs to perform additional judgment work during the flight based on this information, it will increase the pilot's workload. Therefore, it is essential to correctly and efficiently utilize the aircraft's own information, obtain the status information of the aircraft from the instrument information to predict potential risks, and provide prompts to the pilot. Currently, there are many auxiliary flight devices for aircraft, which mainly help pilots better understand and judge the aircraft's condition in different environments.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Effect Intelligent Monitoring for Automatic Stirring Process
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: The stirring with a rotary motion is a highly automatic process in the industrial automation, especially in the chemical, food and pharmaceutical industries. The intense friction and collision between the stirring blade and raw materials (solid granules or liquids) can produce an obviously electrostatic charging effect, especially in dry environment. The unexpected discharging can ignite dust clouds. In this paper, we presented the real-time monitor methods for both charging strength and discharging event. Experiment results showed that the maximum potential of 20.61 kV was obtained at 9 cm from the bottom wall by the designed potential transfer measurement. The discharge leakage current of microseconds was detected across the designed high-speed current circuit while it was connected to the grounded wall of stirring drum. Those proposed sensing methods is capable of early prevention of electrostatic hazards in the field of automatic stirring process.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Spatiotemporal Analysis of Air Quality Based on Big Data
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: It adopts a multidimensional spatiotemporal analysis method to analyze the temporal distribution and spatial distribution characteristics of haze pollution from the dimensions of time and space in Chengdu. Through the analysis of real-time data from six air monitoring points over the past three years in Chengdu, it is concluded that the frequency of haze pollution is higher in December and January, and the air quality is relatively poor inside the city compared to outside the city. In addition, adopting a multi criteria perspective to display the changes of air quality in a certain region or time period can discover potential patterns of spatiotemporal changes in air quality, and provide auxiliary decision-making support for formulating long-term prevention and control strategies under different spatiotemporal conditions.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electric Field on the Surface of Fittings and Main Equipment Inside ± 800kV UHV Converter Valve Hall Based on the Finite Element Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: The valve hall in a UHV converter station serves as the hub of a UHV DC transmission project. When operating normally, it adheres to rigorous standards concerning the surface electric field of its internal fittings. Consequently, during the design phase of the valve hall, it is crucial to calculate and validate the electric field strength on the surface of these fittings to guarantee that it remains beneath the corona field strength for each piece of equipment. In this paper, the simulation calculation of the high-end valve hall fittings of a UHV DC transmission project ± 800kV converter station is carried out. The numerical calculation method of the surface electric field of the UHV DC valve hall fittings is studied. The whole model of the valve hall equipment is established to calculate and analyze the electric field. The distribution characteristics of the surface electric field when the valve hall equipment is working are obtained, and the maximum surface field strength of each fitting in the valve hall is found. Analyze whether it is dizzy, study the distribution law of its surface field strength, and check the performance of shielding fittings.

articleTitle: Rapid Assembly Method of Large Volume Stone for Transportation Facilities Based on BIM
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Nowadays, in order to meet the needs of traffic facilities for landscape, stone is widely used in municipal engineering sidewalk paving. However, the phenomenon of stone cutting caused by the mismatch between the stone size and the station area often occurs in the actual project, which increases the construction cost and affects the construction efficiency, and does not meet the strategic needs of the sustainable development of today's society. Aiming at the above problems, this paper puts forward a rapid assembling method of railway yard stone based on BIM technology. By analyzing the characteristics of the blanking problem, the assembly area is regarded as the base material, the stone is regarded as the sub-material, and the stone loss of the boundary of the assembly area is considered in the actual assembly process. The four-point adaptive stone family is constructed by using Revit conceptual volumetric method, and the parametric assembly of traffic facilities stone based on BIM is realized by Dynamo visualization program editor. Finally, taking a certain area of a traffic facilities in Xi 'an City as an example, by calculating and comparing the boundary loss of the stone combination with six different sizes, the optimal stone combination is selected to carry out BIM parametric assembly. The research results show that the stone assembly method proposed in this paper can effectively improve the construction efficiency, improve the degree of engineering refinement, and reduce the construction cost.

articleTitle: Research on Aircraft Automatic Drilling and Riveting Task Planning and Simulation Technology Based on DELMIA
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Based on the application content, scope, and process of digital enterprise lean manufacturing interactive application (DELMIA), conduct research on aircraft automatic drilling and riveting task planning and simulation technology. Establish a process numerical model for the product, study the optimal path planning for the assembly process, achieve automatic planning of robot drilling and riveting tasks, and generate numerical control (NC) code for robot execution. Virtual simulation of robot automatic drilling and riveting tasks based on DELMIA, conducting assembly interference inspection, and achieving advance planning and simulation of production assembly tasks. Verify the effectiveness and accuracy of automatic drilling and riveting task planning and simulation methods through examples. The results indicate that the hole position error after processing is controlled within 0.3mm, which can meet the requirements of hole making.

articleTitle: Construction of Underwater Sound Field Propagation Loss Simulation Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Firstly, based on the netCDF data set and the formula of sound velocity profile, the sound velocity profile data of each position in the ocean is successfully calculated. Secondly, by incorporating the velocity profile data into various models of underwater sound field propagation loss, we can derive propagation loss data calculated by different models. Thirdly, the application scenarios of various propagation loss models are introduced in detail, along with the significance of propagation loss data based on the sonar equation. Finally, from an engineering application perspective, these sound field propagation models are calculated using a C++ program. All of the aforementioned models were simulated using the Qt platform and the open-source tool QCustomPlot. These models are then integrated into the software package. The application prospect of this software involves evaluating sonar performance and hydrological systems under complex sea states.

articleTitle: Economic Optimal Scheduling of Microgrids Based on Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Microgrids, as independent and controllable power systems, are key to integrating renewable energy sources. However, the stochastic nature of renewables and load fluctuations complicates dispatch modeling. This study addresses system uncertainties by developing a two-level stochastic programming model with compensation and proposes a model predictive control (MPC)-based algorithm to solve it. Simulation results show that the proposed method reduces operating costs by 10.9% compared to traditional deterministic models, demonstrating improved operational economy and practical application potential.

articleTitle: Pedestrian Positioning Algorithm Based on Zero-Velocity Correction
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Pedestrian positioning technology is a key technology that has emerged in recent years in the field of navigation. It is of great significance in indoor, underground and other navigation fields. In this paper, aiming at the problem of error accumulation in pedestrian positioning systems based on MEMS devices, a pedestrian positioning method based on the inertial navigation scheme is studied, and the zero-velocity correction method is used to suppress the accumulation of velocity errors, thereby improving the positioning accuracy. The effectiveness of the method in this paper is verified by experiments.

articleTitle: Robot Teleoperation via Virtual Reality: A Unity and ROS Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of virtual reality (VR) with teleoperation systems to enhance human-robot interaction. With the rise of remote operations, traditional methods often rely on two-dimensional interfaces, making it challenging to control robots in complex three-dimensional environments. This research presents a VR teleoperation system using the Meta Quest 2 headset, enabling immersive control of a climbing robot with six degrees-of-freedom and magnetic adhesion. The system architecture integrates Unity for virtual simulation and the Robot Operating System (ROS) for real-time communication and control. A virtual environment allows the user to control the virtual robot model through the VR headset and controllers, with ROS serving as the communication bridge between the virtual and physical robots, enabling effective operations in various applications, including high-risk environments (A video is available at https://youtu.be/MiZDOV4IfLA).

articleTitle: RANS Model-based Constant Temperature Anemometry Examination to Validate Negligible Wind Tunnel Blockage Effect on Developed Multi-scale Generated Grid Turbulence
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: The aim of this study is to quantitatively assess the effect of wind tunnel blockage on multi-scale generated turbulence and to analyze the results in comparison with the results of previous studies. In particular, the study focuses on the mainstream weak acceleration phenomena and their turbulence characteristics, and the effects are evaluated using acceleration parameters. The decay exponent calculated by introducing a turbulence time scale was larger than the results in the previous study for square lattice turbulence, indicating a rapidly decaying field. An evaluation of the dependence on flow velocity was also carried out, and the results obtained by varying the set flow velocity confirm that the effect of acceleration on turbulent energy, dissipation rate, length scale and time scale is independent of flow velocity. Compared to the measurement uncertainty, the effect of acceleration was small and no statistically significant differences were found. The results of this study provide important information for the quantitative assessment of the impact of weak acceleration phenomena in the main flow due to blockage effects in the wind tunnel test section on multi-scale generated turbulence.

articleTitle: Track Prediction Method of Unmanned Platform Based on Reinforcement Learning and Improved Potential Field Method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In the modern battlefield environment, unmanned platforms and unmanned clusters are playing an increasingly important role, and the analysis and prediction of unmanned platform behavior and command and control have become a hot research topic. In this paper, the track parameters of the unmanned platform in a continuous time period are used as sample data, and the historical track of the unmanned platform is fitted by the function fitting method. Based on the static obstacle information and dynamic obstacle information in the application scene, the corresponding repulsion field is constructed. Based on the empirical playback training network model, the trained network model is finally used to predict the track of the unmanned platform in the future. Simulation experiments show that this method can significantly improve the training efficiency of the unmanned platform track prediction model and the accuracy of the prediction results.

articleTitle: Implementation of Rao-Blackwellized Particle Filter on LIMO ROS2
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is crucial for autonomous mobile robots navigating unknown environments. Traditional methods like Extended Kalman Filters and Particle Filters manage uncertainties but often falter in dynamic settings. This article discusses the implementation of the Rao-Blackwellized Particle Filter (RBPF) in the SLAM system of the LIMO ROS2 platform. By integrating RBPF into the default ROS2 framework, we decompose the SLAM problem into simpler sub-problems, enhancing computational efficiency and estimation accuracy. Results show that the implemented system effectively handles dynamic environments and noisy data, as demonstrated through simulations and real-world experiments with the LIMO ROS2 robot.

articleTitle: Wave-Bottleneck: an Enhanced Architecture for Decreasing Parameters in Deep Network Models
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: The field of computer vision has seen remarkable advancements with deep neural networks, particularly the ResNet architecture, which effectively reduces the number of parameters and addresses the vanishing gradient problem through its Bottleneck block design and skip connections. In this study, we strive to further reduce network parameters while safeguarding model precision by introducing the Wave Bottleneck. This groundbreaking integration seamlessly merges the Bottleneck block with Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT). Wave Bottleneck leverages DWT for feature decomposition and reconstruction, combining 1D and 2D DWT to enhance computational efficiency. Our method performs feature extraction on the input data in the channel domain to efficiently and effectively capture the correlation and important features between channels. Moreover, we realize important feature extraction in the spatial domain by performing feature extraction. Extensive experiments on standard datasets show that Wave Bottleneck outperforms traditional ResNet models in terms of accuracy and parameter reduction, showcasing its potential for deployment in resource-constrained environments.

articleTitle: Optimization Machining Processes in Multi-User Cyber-Physical Cells: A Comparative
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This article presents the virtual commissioning of a multi-user cyber-physical laboratory for remote access (Multicyber) integrated with Industry 4.0 technologies to promote neoindustrialization. The project incorporates Digital Twins, Virtual and Augmented Reality, Artificial Intelligence, Industrial Robotics, Vision Systems, Autonomous and Collaborative Robots, Cybersecurity, and the Industrial Internet of Things. The objective of the Multicyber project is to create a demonstration center focused on advancing applied research in manufacturing processes. The laboratory features a manufacturing cell with an Autonomous Mobile Robot (AMR), a collaborative anthropomorphic manipulator (cobot), quality inspection via computer vision, a five-axis machine, and a robotic arm for machining. This study presents the simulation of three complete manufacturing routines. Plant Simulation software was used to obtain travel times for the AMR, inspection, and part removal stages, while NX software was used for detailed machining simulations with precision adjustments. The results highlight the benefits of using robotic arms in manufacturing and demonstrate how AMRs and cobots can add value through the planning and integration of routines.

articleTitle: Dynamic Voxel-Based Lidar Inertial Fusion SLAM Algorithm for Denial Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: To solve the problem of vehicle location mapping limitation in urban canyons, tunnels, and other low-texture, low-light, and high-dynamic denial scenes, a dynamic voxel-based lidar inertial fusion SLAM algorithm DSC-Algo for denial scenes is proposed. The algorithm introduces a dynamic voxel data structure to maintain the local map and nearest neighbor search, which can efficiently insert and delete new lidar points, to improve the computational efficiency of the algorithm. At the same time, the pose optimization method of factor map was used to introduce the loop detection factor of scan-context descriptors that could reflect the three-dimensional structure characteristics of the point cloud, and the objective function including odometer factor, IMU pre-integration factor and the error term of scan-context environment loop detection factor was constructed. The optimal pose state was solved by a nonlinear optimization algorithm, and the positioning accuracy was improved. A complete SLAM algorithm framework is constructed by odometry algorithm, factor graph optimization, and loop closure detection. Compared with the mainstream lidar inertial SLAM algorithm FAST-LIO2, the computational efficiency of the proposed DSC-Algo algorithm in the iterative Kalman filtering stage and point cloud distortion removal stage is improved by nearly 40%. The test results of real vehicles in the reality denial scenario of the underground parking lot and urban tunnel show that DSC-Algo algorithm has higher positioning accuracy and more accurate mapping effect than the FAST-LIO2 and LeGO-LOAM algorithms.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Algorithm Based Scheduling Method for Flexible Production Line
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: The State Council in “Made in China 2025” clearly put forward to vigorously promote the integration of information technology and industrialization, to achieve technological breakthroughs in key areas in aerospace equipment. In the next decade, China's demand for aircraft will continue to increase, which requires high manufacturing efficiency and fast response speed of aircraft parts. However, in actual production, the research and application of the production line scheduling algorithm is still relatively small, which leads to the actual production cannot play out the maximum efficiency of the production line. In view of the above problems, this paper takes the actual flexible production line as the research object, establishes the scheduling model in line with the actual production on the spot, and uses the optimized particle swarm algorithm to solve the model, to obtain the optimal solution to meet the requirements of the actual scheduling, so as to give full play to the maximum efficiency of the production.

articleTitle: Bringing Two Worlds Together: The Convergence of Large Language Models and Knowledge Graphs
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed numerous fields with their strong capabilities in generalization and inference, yet they face challenges such as dependence on probabilistic reasoning, lack of factual knowledge, and limited interpretability. Knowledge Graphs (KGs), with their structured factual information, can address these gaps by providing external knowledge, though they also struggle with issues like scalability and representing new or unseen facts. Integrating LLMs and KGs offers a complementary solution, as both can mutually enhance each other. This article categorizes and reviews three main frameworks: (1) LLM-enhanced KGs, where LLMs support KG tasks like embedding, completion, and question answering; (2) KGenhanced LLMs, which integrate KGs to improve LLMs' factual understanding; and (3) Collaborative KGs and LLMs, where both systems interact symbiotically, enabling bidirectional reasoning. We review representative methods, analyze current limitations, and discuss future research directions and applications.

articleTitle: Inverse Linear Quadratic Regulator Problem for Discrete-Time Systems via LMI
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the inverse optimal control problem for discrete-time systems with unknown cost functions using linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Based on Pontryagin's minimum principle, a novel model-based algorithm is proposed to reconstruct the weight matrices of an unknown quadratic cost function. This algorithm is formulated using LMIs to find a solution to the algebraic Riccati equation, which is then used to determine the weight matrices. We prove that the solution obtained from LMIs belongs to the set of solutions for the inverse optimal control problem. On this basis, a noniterative model-free algorithm is presented to solve the problem without requiring system matrices. The collected data is used to estimate the unknown weight matrices, and we prove that our algorithm can obtain an approximate optimal solution. Finally, an example illustrates the effectiveness of our algorithms, and comparisons show that our algorithms outperform others.

articleTitle: Research on Robustness and Denoising Based on the H-F Algorithm of the Large-aperture Optical Infrared Telescope
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In this paper, an H-F(<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> ∞ -Filter) control algorithm is proposed to ensure that the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) of the large-aperture optical infrared telescope drive system can operate normally under the condition of high switching noise and extreme large wind-borne disturbances in the control system. The H-F algorithm combines the position loop and the velocity loop controller with the filtering algorithm to form the H-F controller and optimizes the control structure of the telescope drive system to be applied to the large-aperture optical infrared telescope. The telescope drive system is a typical large-inertia, ultra-low-speed, high-precision system, and the robustness of the H-F algorithm is verified by the position tracking form in the arc second range, the influence of switching noise, and the addition of wind-borne disturbance in the experimental process. The superior performance of the H-F algorithm is verified by comparing it with the traditional triple closed-loop PID control.

articleTitle: Energy Optimization Analysis of Robot Trajectories and Optimization Strategies of Processing Tasks Based on Time-Scaling Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Currently, optimizing trajectories is an effective method to reduce energy consumption of robotic manufacturing systems. Nevertheless, energy-efficient trajectory planning of robots has consistently posed a challenge. In this paper, we initially analyzed the energy consumption characteristics of industrial robots in detail. Subsequently, a qualitative analysis was conducted on the systematic modeling process from the general energy consumption model to a time-scaling function-based task energy characteristic model. Furthermore, the influencing factors of task energy coefficients were analyzed in depth, and the energy-saving optimization performance of robotic trajectory modification with time-scaling functions was evaluated via case studies. The results demonstrate that execution time is the primary determinant of energy consumption; moreover, the acceleration and deceleration patterns of end tools also have an influence on energy consumption, but this influence is notably significant in scenarios with shorter execution time only, and is usually smaller than the impact of execution time on energy consumption. Finally, energy-saving optimization strategies of typical processing tasks were proposed after analyzing the optimization hierarchies of robot processing trajectories based on the time-scaling method. This study can provide theoretical bases and technical supports for energy consumption modeling and energy-saving trajectory planning of industrial robots and robotic processing systems.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Metaverse Digital Twin Cities: Prototype Platform Design for Integrated Virtual Urban Ecosystems and Services
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This study presents a cutting-edge platform, meticulously crafted by a multidisciplinary team, designed to actualize Metaverse Digital Twin Cities (Meta-city) and their associated Scene Services. The Meta-city integrates real-world urban services with a virtual CIM platform, offering a novel hybrid experience that merges virtual and real-world services. The platform's architecture is structured into five layers: Perception, Data, Platform, AI Engine, and Metaverse, culminating in an extensive 3D model database that augments the capabilities of traditional smart city frameworks. It targets users with significant urban modeling needs, such as city administrators and residents, providing a multi-dimensional 3D city operation and maintenance model suitable for both administrative and commercial use. This model is complemented by services like real-time rendering monitoring and urban disaster prevention etc., tailored to meet the unique demands of urban stakeholders. The platform's integrated approach is poised to streamline urban governance by leveraging digital twins, thereby revolutionizing the urban experience. The fusion of diverse expertise within the platform ensures a holistic strategy for advancing urban digital ecosystems, potentially redefining smart city technologies. Currently operational in several pilot Chinese cities, this initiative exemplifies the application of theoretical research to engineering practice to enhance urban operations and governance efficiency.

articleTitle: Edge Computing for Industrial Dust Reduction Research Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In complex industrial scenarios, faced with limited computational resources, a large amount of data leads to a high latency problem in dust data processing. Considering the threat of dust pollution and dust explosion to life and health, it is important to prioritize dust data processing. Existing dust reduction methods cannot be dynamically adjusted according to the collected dust data, resulting in low dust reduction efficiency, high energy consumption of equipment, and inability to meet the quality requirements for processing dust. To address the above problems, an optimized multi-objective industrial dust reduction processing method using edge computing is proposed, which is modeled as a constrained multi-objective optimization problem. The task priority is set to ensure that dust tasks can be offloaded first in busy industrial tasks. In order to find the optimal offloading strategy that minimizes task latency and energy consumption, the EHA-SP algorithm, which has both global search capability and parameter adaptation according to task changes, is used to maximize processing efficiency. Experimental results show that the algorithm has significant advantages in reducing latency and minimizing energy consumption. Compared with the original two algorithms, the latency is reduced by 11.8% and 54.57%, and the average energy consumption is reduced by 3.18 percentage points and 0.97 percentage points, respectively, when the number of tasks is 500. The application of edge computing in industrial dust reduction can effectively reduce the time delay and equipment energy consumption, optimize the dust reduction efficiency, reduce the environmental pollution caused by dust, reduce the chances of dust explosion, protect the life safety of industrial producers, and extend the service life of the equipment.

articleTitle: Research on Low Illumination Target Detection Method for Prefabricated Beam Field Based on Retinex
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: There is a problem of low illumination in the video surveillance of the precast beam field, which seriously affects the effect of the intelligent analysis algorithm. Based on the in-depth study of the low-illumination images of beam fields, this paper proposes a decomposition network module based on the encoding-decoding architecture of Retinex theory, which uses the improved U-Net structure to extract features, maps the features to the low-dimensional probability density distribution with the help of normalized streams, and decodes the reflection component features of the input image. The network module is used to replace the feature extraction module of the existing mainstream object detection algorithms, which can significantly improve the recognition effect of the algorithm under low illumination conditions. After embedding the module in the mainstream object detection algorithms YoloV8 and Faster RCNN respectively, the MAP value of object detection remains stable under normal illumination, and the MAP value of object detection is increased by 5% on average under low illumination.

articleTitle: Analyze the User Behaviors via Network Traffic Data in Smart Home
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: As a service medium for household units, smart homes can serve as energy management hubs by analyzing user behavior within the home to optimize energy allocation and usage, thereby avoiding unnecessary resource waste—for example, turning off the TV while the user is taking a shower. However, many users refuse to allow third-party analysis of their smart device data due to privacy concerns. To address this issue, we propose a technique for accurately extracting user behavior features from network traffic, enabling non-intrusive user behavior recognition. Recognizing user behavior poses significant challenges due to the uncertainty of user activities and the encrypted nature of network traffic. To overcome these challenges, we leverage a dynamic time warping (DTW) algorithm to transform encrypted traffic data into device event sequences using device event fingerprints, facilitating the matching of user activity patterns. Furthermore, we introduce a deterministic finite automaton (DFA) model to capture transition rules within activity sequences, enhancing recognition accuracy. We evaluated our approach on a self-constructed real-world dataset, and the experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves a behavior recognition accuracy of up to 87.3%.

articleTitle: Design and Prototyping of an Robotic Exoskeleton for Rehabilitation After Total Knee Arthroplasty
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: The most increasing trend is to utilize total knee arthroplasty (TKA) as a surgical solution to relief the effects of severe arthritis. Researchers have become interested in replacing an efficient robotic assisted method in place of traditional physiotherapy post-TKA. The effectiveness of these devices in reducing recovery time, improving mobility, and decreasing the risk of future injuries is entirely reliant on the design and functionality of the proposed robotic system. The main objective of this study is to propose a streamlined and organized process to design and construct an exoskeletal robotic system for post-TKA, drawing on biomechanical investigations. In the design of a system for safe human-robot interaction during rehabilitation, it is crucial to prioritize compatibility and reliability as important parameters. This research proposes a framework that combines physiotherapy protocol with biomechanical analysis of human motion to address these issues. An experimental investigation was conducted on the built prototype to assess the performance of the suggested design framework.

articleTitle: MER-MFNet: Micro-Expression Recognition Based on Multimodal Fusion Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Micro-expressions (MEs) are brief and subtle facial movements that can reveal hidden emotions. We observe that MEs are manifestations of small localized changes, and deep learning has already played an important role in this area. However, existing studies do not adequately consider the local and global characteristics of the data: apex frames represent global apex features, while optical flow maps reflect localized subtle movements. Therefore, different data modalities require the use of suitable feature extraction network architectures. In this paper, we propose a novel multimodal fusion network for micro-expression recognition (MER-MFNet). The network comprises three components: apex frames feature learning using vision transformers (ViT), optical flow maps feature selection using convolution neural networks (CNNs), and micro-expression (ME) keypoint feature classification. The apex frames and optical flow maps features are fused using a convex combination method, and their similarity is compared. Finally, the combined features are integrated with the keypoint classification results to achieve efficient MER. Experiments on CASME II, SAMM, SMIC-HS and MEGC2019-CD datasets show that MER-MFNet exhibits excellent performance in MER, significantly improving recognition accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Closed-Loop Individual Music Neurofeedback Based on Brain-Computer Interaction for Student Stress Intervention
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Music neurofeedback is a non-invasive method for regulating neural activity and reducing stress based on brain-computer interface technology combined with music stimulation. However, the current music neurofeedback protocol is regulated by a single indicator, resulting in significant differences in individual effects. This study proposed a neurofeedback protocol based on personalized music selection and used three stress scales and two cognitive behavioral experiments to evaluate the stress regulation effect, and combined electroencephalogram (EEG) microstate analysis to explore the stress relief mechanism. Five university students participated in a five-session neurofeedback training. After the intervention, the results of the Depression-Anxiety-Stress Scale (DASS-21) and the Stroop task showed a significant decrease in the scores of stress-related symptoms and a significant improvement in response inhibition. The EEG results showed that the absolute power of the a band in the frontal and temporal lobes increased significantly, the coverage and duration of microstate C decreased significantly, and the duration of microstate D increased significantly, which was significantly correlated with the reduction of stress scores. Personalized music neurofeedback provides a potentially effective tool and innovative perspective for student stress management. The elucidation of spatiotemporal neurocognitive mechanisms provides a new theoretical framework for the development and optimization of neurofeedback protocols.

articleTitle: Advanced Government Chatbot Featuring Multi-Source Strategy for Effective Goal-Driven Dialogues
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Government chatbots (G-chatbots) aim to provide proactive, comprehensive information services, focusing on high-quality consultation rather than just answering queries. Due to the complexity of user questions, multiple dialogue turns are often needed for accurate responses. However, optimal answers in single turns may not align with the user's ultimate goal. To address this, we propose a Multi-Source-Aware algorithm designed for conversation-level objectives in G-chatbots. This algorithm features two key components: the Multi-Source-Aware (MSA) adapter module, which fine-tunes the chatbot's understanding based on user intent, conversation context, and preset knowledge, and the Virtual Edge module, which guides the conversation toward the final goal. Experiments show that this approach improves QA efficiency and answer quality, with fine-tuning using just 0. 01-13% of the parameters, resulting in a 2% increase in question comprehension and a 6% boost in answer quality compared to baseline models.

articleTitle: A Low-cost and Energy-efficient Real-time Speech Isolation Model for AIoT
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In the pursuit of efficient speech processing, deep learning-based denoising models have been hindered by a large number of parameters and high computational intensity. In this paper, we present a novel deep learning-based lightweight time-domain speech denoising model that avoids the computational overhead of the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) used in frequency-domain approaches. The design focus of this model is to achieve real-time processing and small model size while also achieving good speech isolation performance. Inspired by the U-Net architecture, the model uses a downsampling and upsampling strategy to compress and then restore data dimensions, with an encoder-separator-decoder structure at its core. The encoder, consisting of five convolutional modules with different stride lengths, captures a wide range of speech features, which are then refined by a transformer-based separator. The transformer, with its unique self-attention mechanism, is capable of capturing long-range dependencies within the speech signal, a crucial aspect for accurately predicting and separating noise components. This enables the model to better understand the context and relationships within the speech waveform, leading to enhanced noise reduction capabilities. The decoder, employing transposed convolutional layers, achieves high fidelity in speech prediction. This model not only reduces the number of parameters to less than 100K, but also maintains denoising effectiveness, making it viable for use on devices with limited computing power. The results indicate a promising direction for time-domain models in speech processing applications.

articleTitle: End-to-End Speech Recognition of Central Miao Language Based on Wav2Vec 2.0
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Miao, as one of China's minority languages, has a complex phonetic system and limited corpus resources, which makes existing speech recognition methods difficult to meet practical demands. This paper introduces the application of the Wav2Vec 2.0 framework for the first time to perform end-to-end speech recognition for the Miao language. We pre-trained the wav2vec 2.0 model on a large amount of unannotated Miao speech data, and then fine-tuned it with a small amount of annotated data. To advance research in Miao speech recognition, this paper also constructs a new 20-hour Miao speech dataset, DHD, and conducts experiments on it. The experimental results show that, compared to traditional end to end speech recognition methods, the Wav2Vec 2.0-based model achieves a WER of 31.3 % on the Miao speech recognition task, demonstrating a significant improvement. Our method not only provides a new solution for Miao speech recognition but also offers a feasible framework for speech processing of other resource-scarce languages.

articleTitle: A Design of Network Security Model for Power System Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: In view of defects such as high-dimensional and imbalanced data in power network system, which lead to low performance of network security mechanism in detecting network attacks, this article designs a grid network security model based on deep learning algorithm. This model is supposed to improve the power system's capability to detect abnormal information and network attacks in the system by learning historical data and related log information. The article carries out a simulation of the model, the result of which proves that it is helpful for the safety management and stable operation of the power system in terms of attacks detection and prevention.

articleTitle: Participation in Vehicle-to-Grid Systems: Understanding the Role of Technology Awareness, Policy Incentives, and Personal Financial Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: This paper investigates the key factors influencing consumers' willingness to participate in Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology, focusing on the roles of technology awareness, policy incentives, and personal financial gain. Using data from 547 electric vehicle users, we conduct factor and regression analyses to explore how these factors individually and interactively affect customers' V2G participation. Our findings reveal that technology awareness significantly boosts consumer participation, as more informed users are likely to engage with V2G regardless of immediate financial rewards. Policy incentives also play a critical role, with clear and consistent government and organizational support enhancing participation rates. However, personal financial gain shows a more nuanced effect—while compensation is a motivator, excessively high expectations can deter users. Additionally, we identify that strong policy frameworks and increased awareness can reduce the need for high financial incentives, creating a more sustainable pathway for V2G adoption. Based on these findings, we propose policy recommendations aimed at improving consumer education, standardizing incentives, and better aligning financial rewards with realistic expectations to promote broader engagement with V2G technology.

articleTitle: SE(3) Pose Estimation for Simultaneous Localization of Objects and Sensors in Dynamic Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) technology offers considerable advantages for enhancing cognitive abilities for mobile robots, especially under complex, dynamic environments. The creation of robust computer vision methods is essential to optimize the understanding of rigid object motion while ensuring precise localization of sensors or cameras. In this study, we introduce a tightly-integrated SLAM approach (MOT), designed to accurately capture SE (3) pose data for sensors/cameras and motion details of objects in the environment. The method initiates by building a streamlined EKF-tracker to determine and associate the real-time motion states of objects. Then, features are separated into static background and object-specific categories based on both instance mask and state information. Static features facilitate the initialization of camera poses, while dynamic features provide SE(3) pose data for objects under observation. Finally, we introduce a novel graph optimization technique to co-optimize the static 3D landmarks, object landmarks, camera poses, and moving object poses within the scene. The proposed approach has shown effectiveness on the KITTI and OMD datasets.

articleTitle: A Method for Cockpit Human-Machine Interface Assessment Based on Human Error Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: With technological advancements and increased automation, many traditional mechanical failures have been effectively prevented and resolved, but human errors remain difficult to completely avoid. New technologies and highly integrated complex designs are continuously being introduced into the cockpit, presenting new challenges for cockpit operations. Advanced human-machine interface designs that lack consideration for human factors may, paradoxically, increase the risk of operational errors by the crew, affecting operational efficiency and potentially threatening flight safety. Therefore, it is crucial to fully consider human factors in cockpit human-machine interface design, identify potential design traps that may lead to human errors, optimize the design accordingly, and thereby improve crew operational efficiency and flight safety. This paper proposes a systematic, structured assessment method for civil aircraft cockpit human-machine interfaces based on human error analysis. This method analyzes the cockpit human-machine interface by predicting human errors caused by or related to the design and assesses the adequacy and effectiveness of the cockpit human-machine interface in managing crew errors. It aims to help designers identify potential deficiencies in the cockpit human-machine interface design and enables programs to understand and manage potential human error effects, understand the relative risks and uncertainties within the system design, and influence decisions throughout the system lifecycle. And this method is good at standardization of Cockpit HMI human error analysis during CS 25.1302 compliance demonstration practices.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Image Classification with Meta Random Fourier Features Based on Bayesian Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Automation, Robotics and Computer Engineering (ICARCE)
abstract: Deep learning methods rely on large amounts of labeled data, and their highly nonlinear structure limits their wide applicability in the field of small samples. The kernel method has become an effective solution for nonlinear low-data regions. In this paper, a meta-learning network Meta-RFFNet based on convolutional random Fourier feature operators is proposed to improve the generalization ability of deep learning models in small samples and cross-domain classification tasks. It uses random Fourier features to construct deep kernel network, balances the difference of sample distribution by synthetic gradient network, and realizes parametric inference based on empirical Bayesian model. This approach overcomes the dependence of deep learning models on large amounts of labeled data, and provides mathematically interpretable mappings for each layer of the kernel network. Experimental evaluations on mini-ImageNet and CIFAR-FS datasets show that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing standard few-shot classification methods, with classification accuracy of 70.67% and 79.33%, respectively, at 5-shot settings.
